newsitem.title: UK: LME copper races to $2,200, five-month highs.
newsitem.headline: LME copper races to $2,200, five-month highs.

text.p: World copper prices surged to five-month highs late on Monday as fears over critically low stock levels continued to plague the market.
Benchmark three month futures on the London Metal Exchange (LME) rose to $2,200 a tonne bid by 1820 GMT, up $52 from Friday's closing levels and $212, or 11 percent from the lows last week.
Traders said the rise reflected continued concern over the sharp fall in LME stocks in recent weeks.
They already stand at six year lows of just over 100,000 tonnes and a fall of around 5,000 tonnes expected on Tuesday would take them below the big psychological level.
Reports of stronger demand than expected from major importer China this year were underpinning values, as was strong physical demand in the U.S. and the Far East.
While offtake in Europe was still sluggish, the shortage of copper scrap meant the region was facing supply tightness, traders said.
